audit_scope.description: This audit covers both EL and CL logic. The subgraphs describe CL-side PeerDAS (custody, sampling, reconstruction), EL-side block size limits (EIP-7934), cross-layer sparse blobpool networking (EIP-8070), and the Fusaka meta-fork coordination (EIP-7607).

out_of_scope: Fork Choice (not covered in these subgraphs)
State Transition (not covered in these subgraphs)

judging.severity_measurement: Impact on the entire Ethereum network
judging.poc_requirement_note: All submissions (except informational) must include an executable coded proof of concept at the time of submission

eips: EIP-7594: PeerDAS - Peer Data Availability Sampling
EIP-7823: Set upper bounds for MODEXP
EIP-7918: Blob base fee bounded by execution cost
EIP-7934: RLP Execution Block Size Limit
EIP-7935: Set default gas limit to XX0M
EIP-7951: Precompile for secp256r1 Curve Support

engine_api.description: EL-CL communication via Engine API is authenticated using JWT and considered semi-trusted
engine_api.rationale: Co-located EL and CL clients communicate via authenticated Engine API (JWT). The Engine API is considered a trusted boundary, but data returned by EL may not be fully verified by CL in all cases (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 is used without KZG verification). If the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data may be propagated to the network.
security_implications: Engine API is authenticated via JWT
Some data from EL may be used without full verification by CL
Compromised EL can affect CL behavior
engine_api.note: Vulnerabilities in Engine API implementation are in-scope, but attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity

local_validator.description: Local validator configuration is under operator control and considered semi-trusted
local_validator.rationale: Local validator configuration is under operator control. Misconfigured or manipulated validator settings could cause incorrect node behavior.
local_validator.note: Configuration issues requiring operator error are typically out-of-scope

p2p_peers.description: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and considered untrusted
p2p_peers.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. All P2P input must be fully validated.
p2p_peers.note: Vulnerabilities exploitable via P2P network are high priority for bug bounty

Critical.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Exploit an EIP/specification or client bug to easily create an infinite amount of ETH which is finalized by the network
Take down the entire network by sending a single malicious on-chain transaction that ends up crashing all clients
Critical.impact: Entire network (>50% validators or all clients)
Critical.attack_vector: Single malicious on-chain transaction or network packet

High.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 33% of the network
Bring down more than 33% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
High.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Medium.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 5% of the network
Bring down more than 5% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Medium.impact: More than 5% of the network (or >1% of validators for slashing)
Medium.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Low.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting at least 0.01% of the network
Bring down more than 0.01% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Low.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

el_attack_vectors.threat: Send oversized blocks exceeding MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE, malformed eth/71 messages (GetCells, NewPooledTransactionHashes with invalid cell_mask), invalid blob transactions
Eclipse attacks to isolate nodes, send invalid blocks/transactions, selective data withholding in sparse blobpool

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Send malformed DataColumnSidecars with invalid KZG proofs, invalid column indices, or corrupted commitment inclusion proofs
Respond with invalid column data to sampling requests, withhold columns to degrade data availability
Generate node IDs to dominate custody of specific columns, then withhold data to break reconstruction

misclassified_entities.reason: EIP-7607: Client implementation teams are part of the development process, not runtime external entities that send data into the system. They are relevant to governance, not to runtime trust boundaries.
EIP-7607: Network operators run the nodes themselves. They are the system operators, not external entities sending data into the system at runtime.
EIP-7607: Core developers participate in governance and specification, not runtime data flow.
EIP-7607: EIP authors participate in the specification process, not runtime data flow.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Gossip (DAS Column Sidecars)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any node can join gossip subnets and publish DataColumnSidecars. All data must be validated: format checks, commitment inclusion proofs, and KZG cell proofs before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Req/Resp (DAS Column Requests)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers responding to direct column data requests are unauthenticated. Responses must be validated with KZG proofs. Peers may withhold data or return invalid columns.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate blocks via P2P. Blocks must be validated for RLP size (MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE = 8 MiB per EIP-7934) before expensive processing to prevent DoS.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via eth/71 (Transaction Announcements)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers announce blob transactions with cell_mask bitmaps. The cell_mask must be validated (nil when no type-3 TXs, or valid B_16 bitmap). Malicious announcements can trigger unnecessary fetches.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via eth/71 (Cell Provider)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Provider peers respond to GetCells requests with cell data. Responses must be validated per EIP-7594 (KZG proofs). Providers may selectively withhold data; noise columns are used for detection.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Subnet Peers (Reconstruction Re-gossip Recipients)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip subnets (outbound re-gossip of reconstructed columns)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: After matrix reconstruction, reconstructed columns are re-gossiped. Receiving peers are untrusted and may amplify or drop data.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received DataColumnSidecars must be validated: (1) column index within [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS), (2) cell count matches expected, (3) commitment_inclusion_proof valid against signed block header, (4) KZG cell proofs valid against commitments. Invalid data must be rejected and peer may be penalized.
Column data received via Req/Resp must undergo identical validation as gossip-received data (format, inclusion proof, KZG proofs). Missing or invalid responses must trigger peer scoring penalties.

Block RLP size must be checked against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) early in the validation pipeline, before expensive operations like signature verification, to prevent resource exhaustion DoS.

cell_mask field must be validated: nil when batch contains no type-3 transactions, or a valid B_16 bitmap otherwise. Malformed cell_mask must cause message rejection. Announcement flooding must be rate-limited.

Cell data from providers must be validated per EIP-7594 KZG specifications. Noise column (C_extra=1) must be checked to detect selective withholding. Providers failing noise checks must be flagged and potentially disconnected.

Reconstructed columns exposed to the network must be treated identically to originally received columns. Re-gossip must only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to. Receiving peers will independently validate.
